advances:
Gives the sharp reflected-envelope inequality with three unequal escape
depths.  It also uses the full fixed \(Q\)-cap mass
\(5|Q|/36\), rather than mere cap nonemptiness, to move every reflected
truncation inward by an explicit positive amount in John position.

In particular, if \(r=|\Delta|\), \(a_i=-\min_K\lambda_i\), and
\(p\) is the area of the reflected \(P_\varnothing\)-cell, then
\[
p<r\,\Omega(a_1,a_2,a_3),
\]
where, after ordering \(a_{(1)}\leq a_{(2)}\leq a_{(3)}\) and putting
\(A=a_1+a_2+a_3\),
\[
\Omega(a_1,a_2,a_3)=
\begin{cases}
2A^2-4(a_1^2+a_2^2+a_3^2),
 &a_{(3)}\leq a_{(1)}+a_{(2)},\\[1mm]
8a_{(1)}a_{(2)},
 &a_{(3)}\geq a_{(1)}+a_{(2)}.
\end{cases}
\]
The two formulas agree on the boundary.  Thus \(p\geq k\) forces the
sharp vector low-occupancy condition
\[
k<r\,\Omega(a_1,a_2,a_3).
\]
For \(a_1=a_2=a_3=a\), this is \(k<6a^2r\).  The result does not yet
derive the opposite occupancy inequality from
\(|K\cap\{\lambda_i\geq0\}|/k\to4/9\); it isolates that as the remaining
bridge and records the additional dominant-width residual branch which
a common-\(a\) argument misses.
author: /root/mp_r55_escape_envelope
proof:
First derive the symmetric thresholds occurring in the canonical
escape.  In the notation of accepted fact `d1177b21864bbcc6`, put
\[
\lambda_i=\gamma(\alpha_i-t_i),
\qquad
\beta_i=-\Lambda_i.
\tag{23}
\]
Since \(t_i=-\Lambda_i/\gamma\), one has
\(\sum_i\lambda_i=1\).  Its exact threshold identities become
\[
Q:\lambda_i\geq-\beta_i,\qquad
R:\lambda_i\geq0,\qquad
P:\lambda_i\geq\beta_i.
\tag{24}
\]
Thus \(P_\varnothing\) satisfies (3), while the three positive
doubleton \(Q\)-caps satisfy the sign condition in (4).
The same accepted fact gives, after John normalization,
\[
B_2\subseteq Q\subseteq2B_2,
\qquad
|C_i|=\frac5{36}|Q|.
\tag{25}
\]
The positive middle singletons imply \(\Delta\subseteq K\) by accepted
fact `e1361027c1dda6fa`.  The height shear used to choose the relative
translation gauge preserves compatibility and all planar areas by
accepted fact `ecee03aff61db31e`, so it does not affect the argument.

Fix \(i\).  Choose \(q_i\in C_i\) minimizing \(\lambda_i\).  For every
\(x\in P\), compatibility and (5) give
\[
-a_i
\leq\lambda_i\left(\frac{x+q_i}{2}\right)
=\frac{\lambda_i(x)-\beta_i-\delta_i}{2}.
\]
This is exactly (6).

The cap \(C_i\) lies in the strip between the parallel lines
\[
\lambda_i=-\beta_i-\delta_i,
\qquad
\lambda_i=-\beta_i.
\]
The Euclidean width of this strip is \(\delta_i/|g_i|\).  Its
orthogonal projection in the direction parallel to the strip has length
at most
\[
\operatorname{diam}(Q)\leq4.
\]
Fubini's theorem, or containment in the corresponding rectangle, gives
\[
|C_i|\leq\frac{4\delta_i}{|g_i|}.
\]
Use (25) and \(|Q|\geq\pi\) to obtain (7).  This is the point where the
exact cap fraction \(5/36\), rather than cap existence, enters.

For \(x\in P\), set
\[
x_i=\beta_i-\lambda_i(x).
\tag{26}
\]
Equations (3) and (6) give
\[
0<x_i\leq u_i,
\qquad
x_1+x_2+x_3=s.
\tag{27}
\]
If some \(u_i\leq0\), (27) has no positive-area solution.  Otherwise,
the affine map \(\lambda\mapsto x\) is a translation followed by
reflection in the plane \(\sum\lambda_i=1\), so it preserves area.
The unrestricted simplex
\[
\{x_i\geq0,\ \sum_i x_i=s\}
\]
has area \(rs^2\): it is the image of \(\Delta\) by a homothety of
ratio \(s\), followed by a translation and a reflection.

Apply inclusion-exclusion to the three violations \(x_i>u_i\).  After
translating \(x_i\) down by \(u_i\), a single violation has area
\(r(s-u_i)_+^2\); intersections of two and three violations give the
remaining terms in (9).  Therefore the entire box section in (27) has
area \(r\Phi_u(s)\).  Since \(P\) is contained in this section, (10)
follows.  Cutting-line strictness changes no area.

It remains to maximize the exact formula.  Put
\(u_{(1)}\leq u_{(2)}\leq u_{(3)}\) and \(U=\sum_i u_i\).
The reflection
\[
x_i\longmapsto u_i-x_i
\tag{28}
\]
maps the section at level \(s\) to the section at level \(U-s\).
Hence \(\Phi_u(s)=\Phi_u(U-s)\).

Suppose first that \(u_{(3)}\geq U/2\).  On
\(0\leq s\leq U/2\), the derivative of \(\Phi_u/2\) is
\[
s-(s-u_{(1)})_+-(s-u_{(2)})_+
+(s-u_{(1)}-u_{(2)})_+.
\tag{29}
\]
It equals, successively,
\[
s,\qquad
u_{(1)},\qquad
u_{(1)}+u_{(2)}-s,\qquad
0,
\]
on the intervals cut out by
\[
0,\ u_{(1)},\ u_{(2)},\
u_{(1)}+u_{(2)},\ U/2.
\]
It is nonnegative.  Thus the maximum is the plateau
\[
u_{(1)}+u_{(2)}\leq s\leq u_{(3)},
\]
and direct substitution gives
\[
\max_s\Phi_u(s)=2u_{(1)}u_{(2)}.
\tag{30}
\]

Now suppose \(u_{(3)}\leq U/2\).  No double-violation term is active
for \(s\leq U/2\), because
\[
u_{(1)}+u_{(2)}=U-u_{(3)}\geq U/2.
\]
The derivative of \(\Phi_u/2\) is therefore
\[
s-\sum_i(s-u_i)_+.
\tag{31}
\]
On the four intervals cut out by the ordered \(u_i\), it is
\[
s,\qquad
u_{(1)},\qquad
u_{(1)}+u_{(2)}-s,\qquad
U-2s,
\]
and is again nonnegative up to \(U/2\).  Symmetry (28) shows that the
maximum occurs at \(s=U/2\).  Substitution gives
\[
\max_s\Phi_u(s)
=\frac{U^2}{2}-\sum_i u_i^2.
\tag{32}
\]
Equations (30)-(32) prove (11)-(12)'s exact maximum formula.

In the balanced branch,
\[
\Psi(u)
=\frac{U^2}{6}
-\sum_i\left(u_i-\frac U3\right)^2
\leq\frac{U^2}{6}.
\tag{33}
\]
In the dominant branch,
\[
\Psi(u)=2u_{(1)}u_{(2)}
\leq\frac{(u_{(1)}+u_{(2)})^2}{2}
\leq\frac{U^2}{8}<\frac{U^2}{6}.
\tag{34}
\]
Thus equality in the universal bound occurs exactly when all three
coordinates are equal.  This proves (12)-(13).

The piecewise formula (11) is nondecreasing in every coordinate and is
strictly increasing in each of its two nondominant coordinates.  Since
(7) decreases all three coordinates by a positive amount, (14) and
(13) give (15).  Substituting \(u_i=2a_i\) into (11) gives the displayed
formula for \(\Omega\).  Equations (16)-(19) follow from
(30), (32), and (33).  Finally, \(p\geq k\) and (15) give the asserted
low-occupancy residual condition.  Compactness of the normalized
parameters in the sharp inequalities (7), (12), and (33) gives
(21)-(22).  This proves the lemma.
statement:
Work in an affine plane with nonconstant affine coordinates
\[
\lambda_1+\lambda_2+\lambda_3=1,
\qquad
\Delta=\{\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\lambda_3\geq0\},
\qquad r=|\Delta|>0.
\tag{1}
\]
Let \(Q,K\) be two-dimensional compact convex bodies and let \(P\) be a
convex set of positive area \(p\).  Assume
\[
B_2\subseteq Q\subseteq2B_2,
\qquad
\Delta\subseteq K,
\tag{2}
\]
where \(B_2\) is the Euclidean unit disk in the John-normalized common
plane.  Let \(\beta_1,\beta_2,\beta_3\) satisfy
\[
P\subseteq\{\lambda_i<\beta_i\text{ for }i=1,2,3\}.
\tag{3}
\]
For every \(i\), let \(C_i\subseteq Q\) be a compact convex cap, up to
cutting-line boundaries, such that
\[
C_i\subseteq\{\lambda_i\leq-\beta_i\},
\qquad
|C_i|=\frac5{36}|Q|,
\qquad
\frac{P+C_i}{2}\subseteq K.
\tag{4}
\]
These are exactly the closures of the three positive doubleton
\(Q\)-caps in the all-double support.  Define
\[
a_i=-\min_K\lambda_i\geq0,
\qquad
\delta_i=-\beta_i-\min_{C_i}\lambda_i>0,
\tag{5}
\]
and let \(g_i\) be the linear part of \(\lambda_i\), viewed as a
Euclidean vector in the John plane.

Then compatibility strengthens the existence-only support bound to
\[
\lambda_i(x)\geq\beta_i+\delta_i-2a_i
\qquad(x\in P),
\tag{6}
\]
and the fixed cap masses give
\[
\boxed{\qquad
\delta_i\geq\frac{5|Q|}{144}|g_i|
\geq\frac{5\pi}{144}|g_i|
\qquad(i=1,2,3).
\qquad}
\tag{7}
\]

Put
\[
u_i=2a_i-\delta_i,
\qquad
s=\beta_1+\beta_2+\beta_3-1.
\tag{8}
\]
Positive area of \(P\) forces \(u_i>0\) and \(0<s<u_1+u_2+u_3\).
For \(t_+=\max\{t,0\}\), define
\[
\begin{aligned}
\Phi_u(s)
={}&s_+^2-\sum_i(s-u_i)_+^2
+\sum_{i<j}(s-u_i-u_j)_+^2\\
&-(s-u_1-u_2-u_3)_+^2.
\end{aligned}
\tag{9}
\]
Then the exact reflected-envelope bound is
\[
\boxed{\qquad p\leq r\,\Phi_u(s).\qquad}
\tag{10}
\]

For any nonnegative vector \(u\), write
\(u_{(1)}\leq u_{(2)}\leq u_{(3)}\) and \(U=\sum_i u_i\), and define
\[
\Psi(u)=
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle\frac{U^2}{2}-\sum_i u_i^2,
 &u_{(3)}\leq u_{(1)}+u_{(2)},\\[2mm]
2u_{(1)}u_{(2)},
 &u_{(3)}\geq u_{(1)}+u_{(2)}.
\end{cases}
\tag{11}
\]
The formulas agree when \(u_{(3)}=u_{(1)}+u_{(2)}\), and
\[
\max_s\Phi_u(s)=\Psi(u)
\leq\frac{U^2}{6},
\tag{12}
\]
with equality in the last inequality exactly when
\(u_1=u_2=u_3\).  Consequently,
\[
p\leq r\,\Psi(2a_1-\delta_1,2a_2-\delta_2,2a_3-\delta_3).
\tag{13}
\]
If
\[
\bar u_i=2a_i-\frac{5|Q|}{144}|g_i|,
\tag{14}
\]
then either some \(\bar u_i\leq0\), in which case \(p=0\), or
\[
\boxed{\qquad
p\leq r\,\Psi(\bar u_1,\bar u_2,\bar u_3)
<r\,\Psi(2a_1,2a_2,2a_3)
=r\,\Omega(a_1,a_2,a_3).
\qquad}
\tag{15}
\]
In particular,
\[
\Omega(a_1,a_2,a_3)
\leq\frac23A^2,
\tag{16}
\]
with equality exactly at \(a_1=a_2=a_3=A/3\).

The vector envelope is sharp before the positive cap-depth losses are
inserted.  In the balanced branch
\(a_{(3)}\leq a_{(1)}+a_{(2)}\), its maximizing reflected level is
\[
s=A,
\tag{17}
\]
and the anisotropic loss from the common-depth value is exactly
\[
\Omega(a)
=\frac23A^2-4\sum_i\left(a_i-\frac A3\right)^2.
\tag{18}
\]
In the dominant branch
\(a_{(3)}\geq a_{(1)}+a_{(2)}\), every level
\[
2(a_{(1)}+a_{(2)})\leq s\leq2a_{(3)}
\tag{19}
\]
maximizes the reflected section, whose area factor is
\(8a_{(1)}a_{(2)}\).  Thus a residual sequence with
\(p/k\geq1\) and
\[
\frac{|K\cap\{\lambda_i\geq0\}|}{k}\longrightarrow\frac49
\qquad(i=1,2,3)
\tag{20}
\]
must remain below the exact vector occupancy threshold in (15).  If,
in addition, it approaches the balanced common-depth threshold in the
precise sense
\[
\frac{k}{(2/3)rA^2}\longrightarrow1
\qquad\text{and}\qquad p\geq k,
\]
then it must additionally have
\[
\frac{a_i}{A}\longrightarrow\frac13,\qquad
\frac{\delta_i}{A}\longrightarrow0,\qquad
\frac{s}{A}\longrightarrow1,
\tag{21}
\]
and \(P\) must asymptotically fill the box section in (9).  The fixed
\(5/36\) cap masses and (7) turn the second condition in (21) into the
necessary geometric escape
\[
\frac{\sum_i|g_i|}{A}\longrightarrow0.
\tag{22}
\]
